story.value: The name magnesium comes from Magnesia, a district in the north-eastern region of Greece called Thessalia.
The Scottish chemist Joseph Black recognized magnesium as a separate element in 1755.
In 1808, the English chemist Humphry Davy obtained impure magnesium metal.

uses.value: Cameras, horseshoes, baseball catchers' masks and snowshoes are among the items made from magnesium alloys.
Magnesium oxide is used in some antacids.
A thin film of magnesium fluoride is applied to optical lenses to help reduce glare and reflections.
Magnesium carbonate is added to table salt to prevent caking.
